metadata: document_id, source, page(=unit no.), unit_id, section (section at chunk start), title, pep_type, python_version, status
vectorizer: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX, 384 dims, cosine, pgvector 0.8.7 exact search
hypothesis: Baseline. Small windows keep single facts but cut sentences and mix sections, so coherence and section metadata should be worse than B.
notes: 553 chunks; 61,817 tokens; embed 26.3 s; 4 chunks >256 tokens truncated. Adjudicated (grader-confirmed equivalent evidence, labelled after test was seen): dev 9/16 & 14/16, test 2/6 & 5/6. Coherence 0.9/2; metadata 13/18 (section wrong in 5).

chunking: by_paragraph (paragraphs of the same heading grouped; new heading = new chunk; long paragraphs split at sentences)
metadata: same fields as A (section = source heading of the paragraphs)
hypothesis: Heading/paragraph-aware chunks keep whole ideas, so coherence and metadata improve and retrieval should not get worse (one factor changed vs A: chunking).
notes: 399 chunks; 54,975 tokens; embed 32.0 s; 21 chunks (5.3%) >256 tokens truncated by the model. Adjudicated: dev 6/16 & 12/16, test 3/6 & 5/6. Coherence 1.7/2; metadata 18/18; top-3 would respect the question scope in 2/3 dev, 0/1 test.

chunking: same as B (identical chunks and vectors)
filter: pep_type or python_version equality filter in SQL, only when the question provides one (d13, d14, d15, t05)
hypothesis: Only difference vs B: metadata filter. Should guarantee scope (filter compliance) and help when other documents compete; no effect on questions without a filter.
notes: Chosen strategy (decision recorded in results/strategy_choice.md before test). Filter compliance 3/3 dev, 1/1 test. Filter changed top-3 for d13 and t05 but did not change any strict hit. Adjudicated identical to B.
